h: Rest and holiness at Shabbat Minchah

p: , — "Rest and holiness You have given to Your people"
— we say in the Minchah prayer,
— which is reckoned as corresponding to
— the holiness of Yaakov our father, peace be upon him,
— as is written (in the Tikkunim, Tikkun 18),
— where he reckons the prayers as corresponding to the Avos.
הַיִּחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
— the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Knesset Yisrael,
— and then there is the contentment (naycha)
— of Hashem, blessed be He, as well;
— as it is said of the site of the Mikdash,
, — "This is My resting place for ever," etc.,
— and there is the place of the union
— of Hashem, blessed be He, with Israel.
— This rest He bequeathed to Israel on Shabbat,
— and we mention it in this prayer:
— which is named for the union,

paragraphs.text: Siddur, Shabbat Minchah Amidah, middle blessing: "You are One and Your Name is One … a rest of love and generosity, a rest of truth and faith, a rest of peace, tranquility, quiet and security … Avraham will rejoice, Yitzchak will exult, Yaakov and his sons rest on it." The whole maamar is a commentary on this blessing, phrase by phrase. Printing corrections made silently in the Hebrew of this maamar: u-shechinitei' → u-Shechinteih ("and His Shechinah"); ve-Edin → ve-Eden ("and Eden," as in the Zohar); le-de'ila → di-le'eila ("of above"); u-ve-Mag' → u-va-Gemara ("and in the Gemara"); rabbah ganzim → harbeh genazim ("many treasuries"); be-veisganzei → be-veis genazai ("in My treasure-house"); lo-l-HKBH → lo la-Kadosh Baruch Hu ("the Holy One, blessed be He, has"); sukam → sukkas ("the shelter of"); u-ve-manos → u-mi-banos ("and than daughters"). The abbreviation "K'" in the opening line is read kedushas, "the holiness of" (cf. "the holiness of the Avos" at the end).

paragraphs.text: Parallels: Pri Tzaddik, Chukat 14 — the same reading of the Shabbat Minchah blessing: Minchah and the third meal are Yaakov's (citing the Arizal), "Yaakov and his sons" is the union of Kudsha Brich Hu and Knesset Yisrael, and "You are One" is named for that union (citing Mateh Moshe); adds why Avraham and Yitzchak are named only at Minchah.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 18 (34a): "For there are three prayers on Shabbat, and the fourth is the Musaf prayer. The evening prayer, 'You have sanctified' (Atah kidashta) — this is the lower Shechinah, which is from the left side... The morning prayer, 'Moshe will rejoice in the gift of his portion' (Yismach Moshe) — this is 'the soul of all living' (Nishmat kol chai), which is the supernal Mother... The third prayer, 'You are One and Your Name is One' (Atah Echad) — this is Havayah, the Middle Pillar that holds both of them." The Middle Pillar, Tiferes, is the attribute of Yaakov; hence Rav Tzadok counts the Shabbat Minchah prayer as Yaakov's and as the prayer of the union.

paragraphs.text: Mateh Moshe (R. Moshe Mat of Przemysl), on the Shabbat prayers: the reason the text of the prayer changes through Shabbat is that at night "You have sanctified" corresponds to betrothal (kiddushin), by day "Moshe will rejoice" to the joy of bridegroom and bride, and at Minchah "You are One" to the union (yichud). Rav Tzadok gives the same source in Peri Tzadik, Chukat 14 ("as the early authorities wrote; see Mateh Moshe").

— the blessing "You are holy" was instituted,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג ד עַמּוּד א)

— Therefore they instituted in this prayer
— "A day of rest and holiness You have given to Your people":
— that there were given to Israel as a gift
— and the holiness was fixed for all eternity.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 4a (Vayikra, Ra'aya Mehemna): "'I have come into My garden, My sister, bride' (Song of Songs 5:1) — this is Malchus, Adni. 'I have gathered my myrrh' — this is Chesed, the level of Avraham...; 'with my spice' — this is Netzach, the level of Aharon...; these are the right arm with the right thigh, and two blessings correspond to them: one, 'Shield of Avraham', and the second, Avodah, which is 'Retzeh'. 'I have eaten my honeycomb' — this is Gevurah, the Fear of Yitzchak; 'with my honey' — Hod, the level of David; that is, the left arm with the left thigh. 'I have drunk my wine with my milk' — the Body and the Covenant, Yaakov with Shlomo." The Ra'aya Mehemna sets the Amidah blessings against the sefiros of the Avos: the first two blessings to Avraham and Yitzchak, and the third, "Atah Kadosh", to the Body, Yaakov.

p: — "Yaakov and his sons rest on it":
— Yaakov is a chariot for the Name Havayah,
— and his sons are Knesset Yisrael,
וְהוּא יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ
— and this is the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא
— according to what is written in the Ra'aya Mehemna
, — "He is truth and She is faith"
, — (and this was explained on Bereishis, maamar 10).
— "A rest of peace, quiet and security":
— peace is peace from the accusation of the evil inclination,
— "There is no peace in my bones because of my sin,"
— and of this it is said,
— "I will give peace in the land,
— and you shall lie down with none to make you afraid."
— It is also rest from the agitation
— of the war of the evil inclination,

h: Three treasuries that hang on Atika

p: — And in the Midrash HaNe'elam on this parashah
— "And Eden — in which place is it?" etc.;
— there are the treasuries of good life,
— and the souls of the righteous," etc.
— This is what they said in the Gemara
— and there many things are listed;
— But here he lists only three things
— the treasuries of blessing, the treasuries of peace,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כח עַמּוּד א)

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 125a (Chayei Sarah, Midrash HaNe'elam): "And Eden, where is it? … In Aravot, for we learned: there are the treasuries of good life, blessing and peace, and the souls of the righteous." See Zohar, Chayei Sara 18:143. The printing's ve-Edin is corrected to ve-Eden ("and Eden") from the Zohar. The three treasuries of this maamar come from here.

Elimelech says that weekdays are "merit" but holy Shabbat is "Mazal" (= 78, three Havayahs), corresponding to the three Shabbat meals. Through them the tzaddik draws down life, children and sustenance, which is Rav Tzadok's conclusion that the three treasuries hanging on Atika are merited in the three meals.

(Chassidus) — On "children, life and sustenance depend on Mazal," R. Elimelech says that weekdays are "merit" but holy Shabbat is "Mazal" (= 78, three Havayahs), corresponding to the three Shabbat meals. Through them the tzaddik draws down life, children and sustenance, which is Rav Tzadok's conclusion that the three treasuries hanging on Atika are merited in the three meals.

paragraphs.text: "And they correspond to the three meals of holy Shabbat, and through the tzaddik the three aforementioned are drawn down."
